newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says 20 Japanese banks eye samurai issue.
newsitem.headline: Israel says 20 Japanese banks eye samurai issue.

text.p: The Israeli Treasury said on Wednesday it has been appraached by some 20 Japanese investment banks, among them the biggest in the country, to participate in its planned samurai offering.
Treasury Director-General David Brodet and accountant-general Shai Talmon will visit Japan next week to meet with prospective underwriters, the Treasury said.

Israel plans to raise approximately 20 billion yen, or $150 million, in Japan in the first half of this year as part of its programme to test international markets for Israeli debt and widen borrowing sources.
Israel has already made offerings in the Eurobond and Yankee markets and plans to raise another $200 million in Yankee bonds later this year.
Israel is preparing for the expiry of the U.S. loan-guarantee programme through which it has borrowed $7.35 billion since 1992. The programme expires in October 1998.
The Treasury added that it had chosen the Tokyo law firm Mitusi Yasuda Wani and Maeda to assist it in the samurai offering.
